newsitem.title: USA: Elder care costs U.S. business $29 billion - survey.
newsitem.headline: Elder care costs U.S. business $29 billion - survey.

text.p: Corporate America loses $29 billion each year from the costs of employees providing personal care to sick or elderly relatives, a survey said Wednesday.

The survey, co-sponsored by the Metropolitan Life Insurance Co., said there were about 14.4 million full- and part-time workers who balance work with caregiving. One in four American households includes such a caregiver, who on average is a 46-year-old working woman.

Replacing workers, absenteeism, job interruptions and other factors that hurt productivity cost the nation's businesses $11.4 billion a year, considering full-time workers only. Add in part-timers, and the bill comes to $29 billion annually, the survey said.
The problem is expected to grow as more baby boomers retire, MetLife said, noting there were 76 million American workers in that category who will start turning 65 in 2011.

"It's clear that controlling the cost of caregiving will be one of American business' first major challenges of the 21st century," MetLife Mature Market Group Vice President James Weil said in a statement.
"We hope this study sends an early warning signal to help the country's large and small businesses contend with the emerging crisis."
The survey's results are to be presented to a Senate committee next week.
The survey found that one in 10 caregivers eventually quits; the figure is higher for "intense" caregivers.
-- 11 percent of caregivers take a leave of absence
-- nearly 60 percent of caregivers are late, leave early or take long lunches "regularly"
-- personal phone calls related to caregiving take an hour a week in lost work time
-- about eight out 10 caregivers say their supervisors are sympathetic and provide support, arrange coverage in their absence and provide advice regarding benefits.

The survey, by the National Alliance of Caregiving on behalf of MetLife, interviewed 1,509 people late last year, mainly while they were away from their jobs. The alliance develops programmes for caregivers and professionals.
